about.title: Ferndale Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Ferndale's small-town charm — its historic storefronts along Main Street, the shops near Bluff Street, the walkways off Fairview Drive — comes with uneven boardwalks, aging pavement, and older building entrances that don't always meet modern safety standards. A fall in one of these spots can happen fast: a wet floor with no sign, a broken step, poor lighting in a parking area. Under California law, the property owner or business generally has to have known (or reasonably should have known) about the hazard before they're held responsible for not fixing or warning about it. That's why what happens in the minutes and days after a fall matters so much — photos of the hazard, witness names, and any surveillance footage from the business can make or break a claim. LawProactive doesn't charge you anything to get matched with an independent attorney familiar with these cases. The attorney works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover something.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Time Runs Out

items.title: Notice Is Everything in These Cases
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney knows how to dig up maintenance logs, past complaints, or inspection records that establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation letter out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having nothing.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Have to Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you can still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help make sure your share of blame isn't overstated.

items.question: I fell at a shop near Main Street in Ferndale — do I have a case?
items.answer: It depends on whether the hazard was something the owner knew about or should have caught with reasonable care. Photos of the spot, any receipts or timestamps showing when you were there, and witness information all help. An independent attorney can review the specifics for free through LawProactive.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall, but if a government-owned property was involved, that window is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. Waiting too long can cost you the right to pursue anything at all.

items.question: What if the store denies knowing about the hazard?
items.answer: That's common, and it's exactly why evidence matters — prior complaint records, inspection logs, or surveillance footage can contradict that denial. An attorney can send preservation requests and gather records before they're lost or destroyed.
